name: Review and release the evidence file to the insurer
sector: health care: medical laboratory testing and health services
summary: When every item a life insurer ordered on an applicant (paramedical exam, tele-interview, attending physician statement, lab result or inspection) is complete, a reviewer checks the file before it goes to the underwriter. The reviewer confirms that every item belongs to the same applicant, that the paramedical questionnaire, measurements, ECG and signatures are complete and that attached documents are readable; the system then sends the package in ACORD or the insurer's format, updates the advisor's status screen and queues the items for billing. Most files pass quickly, but missing signatures, unanswered questions, unreadable ECGs or APS pages and untested specimens send files back to examiners, the APS team or the insurer, and those loops make up most of the delay.

baseline.org_archetype: The insurance medical evidence business of a large Canadian laboratory company, closing about 38,000 orders a month for all Canadian life insurers.
baseline.notes: Order management system with ePara electronic paramedical files and iCARE status; ACORD and custom electronic delivery; fax and email still used with clinics and some insurers.

trigger: The last ordered evidence item is attached to the order and the order enters the review queue.
end_state: The evidence package is transmitted to the insurer, the advisor's status is updated and the items are queued for billing, or the order is closed incomplete on the insurer's instruction.

volume.seasonality: Follows life insurance applications: lower in summer and late December.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file's d_insurance_orders driver; one review per order.

systems.name: Insurance Order Management System with Paraweb ordering and iCARE status hub
ePara electronic medical evidence collection on examiner laptops
Electronic results delivery to insurers (ACORD and custom formats)
Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording

steps.name: Move the completed order to the review queue
steps.description: When the last ordered item (paramedical file, tele-interview report, APS, lab result or inspection report) is attached to the order, the order management system marks the order complete and places it in the evidence review queue for its insurer.

evidence.note: The carrier is notified as soon as the order is completed (dyn_para); order status in iCARE (dyn_adv).

steps.name: Run the automated completeness checks
steps.description: The order management system checks the insurer's requirement list against the attached items: required ePara sections and signatures captured, lab result attached, ECG tracing present when ordered, and documents attached as images; files with a gap are flagged.

error.defect_description: A rule misses a missing item.

control.basis: Insurer service agreement requirement specifications for each evidence item

next.condition: APS or inspection only and passes; images need a look
tele-interview or lab items only, already released electronically, and passes

evidence.note: Electronic exam apps flag missing required fields (examone2016); ePara used for paramedical files (dyn_car). Shares are estimates: about 42 percent of orders include a paramedical in the organisation file's volumes; orders whose items were all released electronically by the tele-interview and laboratory workflows close without a reviewer.

steps.name: Open the file and check the applicant's identity across items
steps.description: The reviewer opens the order and confirms the applicant's name, date of birth, policy number and insurer are the same on the paramedical file, lab result, tele-interview and any APS, so no other person's information goes into the package.

error.defect_description: A mismatched item is not noticed.

control.basis: PIPEDA safeguards principle: protect sensitive personal information against unauthorized disclosure

next.condition: item belongs to another applicant or details conflict

evidence.note: Names must be consistent throughout and match the applicant (dyn_kit2020); safeguards against unauthorized disclosure (opc_safeguards). Queue wait and shares are estimates; files completed after hours wait for the morning.

steps.name: Examine a flagged gap
steps.description: The reviewer reads the flag (missing signature, unanswered question, missing ECG, untested lab result, APS pages missing) and decides whether the gap can be fixed from information already held, needs the examiner or APS team, or needs the insurer's decision.

next.condition: lab untested or item cannot be obtained

evidence.note: Common file quality problems on paper and electronic exam forms (examone2016). Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Check the paramedical questionnaire and signatures
steps.description: For files with a paramedical, the reviewer reads the ePara questionnaire for unanswered questions and 'yes' answers without the required details (dates, doctors, medications), and checks the applicant's and examiner's signatures and the consent and authorization.

error.defect_description: A missing detail is passed to the insurer.

control.basis: PIPEDA consent principle: express, signed consent of the applicant to collect and disclose health information to the named insurer

evidence.note: Signed notice and consent by the proposed insured (dyn_kit2020); express consent for sensitive information (opc_consent). Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Check the measurements and the ECG tracing
steps.description: The reviewer checks that height, weight, blood pressure and pulse are recorded and plausible, that repeat blood pressures are present when the first reading was high, and that an ordered ECG tracing is attached with all leads readable.

error.defect_description: Implausible value or unreadable ECG passed.

evidence.note: Paramedical content (measurements, resting ECG) described in dyn_para. Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Ask the examiner for a correction or addendum
steps.description: The reviewer messages or phones the examiner with exactly what is missing (an answer detail, a repeat blood pressure, an ECG resend) and sets the order to pending correction so the advisor sees the status.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Reopen the order for a revisit
steps.description: A case coordinator reopens the order, tells the advisor why (missing signature, wrong applicant's item, ECG must be repeated), and books the examiner to revisit or the applicant to call back; the order returns to review when the new item arrives.

evidence.note: Status shown to advisors in iCARE (dyn_adv). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Check the lab result and other attached documents
steps.description: The reviewer confirms that the lab result is attached and complete or carries a not-tested comment, and that any tele-interview report, APS or inspection report on the order is attached as a readable image with all pages.

evidence.note: Insurers receive lab results electronically (87 percent) and APS, paramedicals and ECGs as images (soa2011). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the examiner's correction
steps.description: The contracted or employed examiner sends an addendum in ePara, resends the ECG tracing, or calls the applicant back to complete an unanswered question, then resubmits the file.

evidence.note: Estimate; most examiners respond within a day or two.

steps.name: Wait for the revisit or new item
steps.description: The applicant is revisited or called back, the new signature, ECG or item is collected and attached to the order, which returns to the review queue.

evidence.note: Outstanding paramedical requirements average 15.2 days to collect across 62 carriers (ipipeline); a revisit on an existing order is assumed shorter, mode three days.

steps.name: Ask the insurer whether to release without the item
steps.description: An account manager emails or calls the insurer's new business contact to ask whether to release the file without the missing item, order a recollection, or cancel that item, and records the decision on the order.

control.basis: Insurer service agreement: incomplete evidence is released only with the insurer's instruction

next.condition: item cancelled or recollection ordered as a new order

evidence.note: The carrier decides whether a recollection is required (dyn_faq). Shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Select files for the pre-release audit
steps.description: The order management system flags a random sample of files, plus files from examiners on a quality watch, for a team lead to audit before release.

control.basis: Company quality assurance sampling of evidence files before release

evidence.note: Vendors run quality assurance on the exam process (examone2016); the 7 percent sample is an estimate.

steps.name: Ask the APS team for missing or unreadable pages
steps.description: The reviewer tells the APS team which pages are missing or unreadable so they can ask the clinic to resend; the order waits.

evidence.note: APS are slow to collect (19.8 days average, ipipeline) and arrive as images (soa2011). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Team lead audits the sampled file
steps.description: The team lead repeats the review against the insurer's checklist and the examiner's quality history, and either passes the file or returns it with the error for correction and examiner feedback.

control.basis: Company quality assurance sampling of evidence files before release

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Release the evidence package
steps.description: The reviewer marks the file reviewed and releases it, which tells the system to build the package in the insurer's format.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the replacement APS pages
steps.description: The APS team asks the attending physician's clinic to fax or upload the missing or clearer pages, and attaches them to the order when they arrive.

evidence.note: Clinics are slow to respond (ipipeline APS averages); the wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Build and transmit the package to the insurer
steps.description: The system assembles the paramedical data, images and any outstanding items into the insurer's ACORD or custom format and sends it through the secure insurer exchange; the insurer's system returns an acknowledgement.

control.basis: PIPEDA safeguards principle: secure transmission of sensitive personal health information

evidence.note: ACORD and customized downloads (dyn_car); images are the most common evidence format (soa2011); safeguards (opc_safeguards). The failure share and batch interval are estimates.

steps.name: Quick-check a file without a paramedical
steps.description: For orders with only a tele-interview, APS or inspection, the reviewer opens the order, confirms the item matches the applicant and is complete, and releases it.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Update iCARE and close the order
steps.description: The order management system marks the order released, shows the status to the advisor and the insurer in iCARE and sends the advisor's notification.

next.condition: insurer later complains about the file

evidence.note: Real-time iCARE status and notification on completion (dyn_adv, dyn_para).

steps.name: Resend or upload a failed package
steps.description: The reviewer checks the insurer exchange error, resends after a fix, or uploads the package to the insurer's secure portal and records the method used.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Queue the order's items for billing
steps.description: The order management system sends each completed item with the insurer's rate (paramedical, kit, ECG, interview, APS fee and any travel surcharge) to client invoicing; items without a rate stop on an exception list.

evidence.note: Per-item billing to insurers is described in the organisation file; exception share is an estimate.

steps.name: Handle an insurer complaint about a released file
steps.description: The director of insurance operations reviews an insurer's complaint about a wrong or incomplete file, has it corrected and resent, and agrees corrective action with the examiner network and reviewers.

control.basis: Company complaint handling and corrective action procedure

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Fix a missing billing rate
steps.description: A case coordinator looks up the insurer's rate card or the approved surcharge, adds the rate and releases the item to invoicing.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Examiner correction
exceptions.description: A paramedical answer detail, repeat blood pressure or ECG is missing and the examiner sends an addendum.

exceptions.name: Revisit needed
exceptions.description: A missing applicant signature, an item from another applicant or a failed correction needs a revisit before release.

exceptions.name: APS pages missing or unreadable
exceptions.description: The APS team must get the clinic to resend pages.

exceptions.name: Insurer decides on an incomplete file
exceptions.description: An untested lab or unobtainable item goes to the insurer, which usually tells the company to release with a note.

exceptions.name: Transmission failure
exceptions.description: The insurer exchange rejects the package and it is resent or uploaded.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the order becoming complete to the package transmitted and the order closed
benchmarks.population: Insurance medical evidence orders at a Canadian evidence provider

evidence.note: No published figure found. The company notifies the carrier as soon as the order is completed (dyn_para); collection of outstanding items is slow (ipipeline), which drives the tail when files reopen.

benchmarks.unit: share of insurer respondents receiving all or virtually all lab results electronically
benchmarks.population: SOA 2010 survey of US and Canadian direct writers

benchmarks.unit: hours or less from lab receipt to carrier

pain_points.description: Gaps found at review (missing answer details, repeat blood pressures, unreadable ECGs) go back to examiners who are contractors in the field, so a small fix can hold a file for a day or more.

evidence.note: Incomplete exam entries are a known quality problem (examone2016); timing is an estimate.

pain_points.description: A missing applicant signature cannot be fixed at the desk and needs a revisit, adding days.

evidence.note: Express consent required (opc_consent); paramedical requirements are slow to collect (ipipeline).

pain_points.description: APS images arrive with missing or unreadable pages and depend on busy clinics to resend.

evidence.note: APS is the slowest requirement (ipipeline).

pain_points.description: Paramedical and APS files are opened by a person even when they passed the system checks, which takes most of the reviewers' time.

evidence.note: Common practice in 2019-2022; estimate.

sources.title: Insurance carriers
sources.supports: Health professionals submit applicant information through ePara on a tablet or laptop; secure online reporting to underwriters; automated data downloads in ACORD and customized formats; order management system with prompts, confirmations and reminders.

sources.title: Insurance advisors
sources.supports: Advisors order online, by email or phone; status updates in real time in the iCARE online order tracking platform; results reported to carriers within 48 hours or less.

sources.title: Paramedical services
sources.supports: The applicant is contacted within 24 to 48 hours and booked within 72 hours; the carrier is notified as soon as the order has been completed; paramedical 25 to 35 minutes, blood profile 20 to 25, resting ECG about 20.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions: The model laboratory's insurance testing service order tracker
sources.supports: Advisors follow order status in the order tracker; specimen results average three business days from collection to the carrier; carriers decide whether a non-viable specimen needs recollection.

sources.title: Instructions for blood/urine kit (insurance), version 6
sources.supports: The proposed insured must read and sign the notice, consent and chain of custody section; the examiner completes all sections and signs; names must be consistent throughout and match the applicant.

sources.title: Report of the Society of Actuaries Improving the New Business Process Survey Subcommittee
sources.supports: 87 percent of insurer respondents received all or virtually all laboratory results electronically; electronic transmission of an image was the most common way of receiving underwriting evidence, in particular APS, paramedicals, ECGs and lab results; 88 percent said the company orders the APS.

sources.title: Five days to issue (iPipeline analysis of outstanding requirements)
sources.supports: Across 62 carriers the average collection time of outstanding requirements is 19.8 days for APS orders, 15.2 days for paramedical exams, 10.3 days for missing application data, 1.4 days for APS review and 1.3 days for data entry; underwriters wait on paramedicals, APS and agent responses.

sources.title: Ask the experts: ensuring quality throughout the applicant exam process
sources.supports: The examiner app is about 70 percent pre-populated from the ordering system and flags missing required fields, reducing unreadable or incomplete paper entries; a quality assurance department reviews applicant feedback daily.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 3: Consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Meaningful consent is required and express consent is generally required for sensitive information; consent can be withdrawn subject to legal or contractual restrictions.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 7: Safeguards
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Personal information must be protected in a way appropriate to its sensitivity against loss, theft and unauthorized access, disclosure, copying, use or modification, through physical, technological and organizational measures.

assumptions: The case is one order and starts when its last item arrives; trigger shares by last item (lab 33 percent, tele-interview 32, APS 21, paramedical without fluids 10, inspection 4) are estimates from the organisation file's volumes.

Tele-interview reports and lab results are also sent to the insurer as soon as they are released (see those workflows); this review covers the order as a whole, the paramedical file and documents, and the closing status and billing.

About 42 percent of orders include a paramedical that gets a full review; APS and inspection files get a quick look at the images; orders with only tele-interview or lab items, already released to the insurer by those workflows, close automatically when they pass the system checks (33 percent).

Hands-on time times volume implies more FTE than stated (see the validator staffing line); the organisation file's 15 evidence reviewers look low for reviewing about 25,000 files a month by hand, so either reviews are faster than estimated or case coordinators and team leads share the review work.
Correction, revisit and APS page rates are estimates; no published rates were found within the search budget.
